important_classification.reason: Each comparison trial starts from a different constrained random high joint configuration before executing the same three-waypoint Cartesian approach.

protocol.approach: same Yunkai Task10 three-waypoint T104 approach
protocol.start_condition: different constrained random high joint configuration

interpretation: Endpoint variation is strongly dominated by the robot-feedback Y direction; X and Z changes are much smaller.
Manual needle-paper displacement agrees extremely strongly with robot-feedback Y displacement, so the large offsets cannot be explained by the ~1 mm manual measurement resolution.
The paper axis recorded as manual X appears to correspond approximately to the RoArm base-frame Y direction. Axis naming must be physically verified before subsequent experiments.
Random starting base-joint angle is strongly associated with final Y displacement. This is evidence of configuration/path dependence, but does not by itself identify the physical cause.
Possible mechanisms to investigate include IK/configuration dependence, backlash/history effects, Cartesian-controller coupling, or other start-state-dependent execution effects.
This dataset must NOT be reported as pure same-start robot repeatability.

next_experiment.name: Same-start robot repeatability
